title: An owned duty survives a lost reply
question: When can cleanup ownership safely end?
scope: The figure’s environment operation, with test termination and durable artifact preservation already verified. Financial settlement is outside this physical cleanup example.

steps.title: Before registration
steps.explanation: No request has left the runtime.

snapshot.result: Provisioning has not started, and no cleanup duty exists yet.

steps.title: Register the cleanup duty
steps.explanation: The coordinator records an unbound duty before dispatch.

snapshot.result: The coordinator now owns an unbound cleanup duty before any external effect.

transition.meaning: The coordinator records an unbound duty before dispatch.

steps.title: Dispatch provisioning
steps.explanation: The recorded duty backs the provisioning request.

snapshot.result: Provisioning is in flight; the already-recorded cleanup duty survives a lost response.

transition.meaning: The recorded duty backs the provisioning request.

steps.title: Record the lost provisioning reply
steps.explanation: Transport termination leaves creation unresolved.

snapshot.result: Creation is unresolved. The coordinator keeps the duty without guessing its target.

transition.meaning: Transport termination leaves creation unresolved.

steps.title: Bind the duty from correlated evidence
steps.explanation: An authenticated result identifies the environment; a lookup guess is insufficient.

snapshot.result: Correlated evidence binds env_r18_01 to the existing duty; ownership remains with the coordinator.

transition.meaning: An authenticated result identifies the environment; a lookup guess is insufficient.

steps.title: Dispatch eligible cleanup
steps.explanation: Both predecessors hold and the duty has a bound target.

snapshot.result: Cleanup is in flight against the verified target after both prerequisites are satisfied.

transition.meaning: Both predecessors hold and the duty has a bound target.

steps.title: Record an unconfirmed release
steps.explanation: The cleanup reply is lost; the environment may be gone or still allocated.

snapshot.result: Release remains unconfirmed. The duty stays owned even though its request timed out.

transition.meaning: The cleanup reply is lost; the environment may be gone or still allocated.

steps.title: Close on authenticated release evidence
steps.explanation: Correlated evidence establishes the declared deallocation postcondition.

snapshot.result: Verified deallocation closes the physical duty; provisioning and release evidence remain visible.

transition.meaning: Correlated evidence establishes the declared deallocation postcondition.

invariants: The cleanup duty is registered before provisioning dispatch.
Unknown outcomes preserve the duty and its owner.
Only correlated release evidence closes the physical cleanup duty; audit history remains.

title: A join waits for its longest branch
question: Why does early lint completion leave synthesis blocked?
scope: Exact hypothetical host-clock intervals from the figure, in seconds. The client timeout and callback are a separate operation, with no clock mapping into these intervals. No task acceptance claim follows.

steps.title: Checks run concurrently
steps.explanation: Retrieval and planning are complete; both independent checks are running.

snapshot.result: Both independent checks run after planning; synthesis waits at their join.

steps.title: Complete lint
steps.explanation: Lint finishes while tests continue to hold the join.

snapshot.result: Lint is done, but unfinished tests still block synthesis.

transition.meaning: Lint finishes while tests continue to hold the join.

steps.title: Complete tests
steps.explanation: The longer branch finishes; synthesis has not started.

snapshot.result: Both checks are complete. The observed synthesis start still lies beyond the unattributed gap.

transition.meaning: The longer branch finishes; synthesis has not started.

steps.title: Start synthesis after the observed gap
steps.explanation: The host records a later start; the intervening interval has no attribution.

snapshot.result: Synthesis begins at its recorded start; these spans do not explain the intervening gap.

transition.meaning: The host records a later start; the intervening interval has no attribution.

steps.title: Complete synthesis
steps.explanation: The response closes the enclosing observation window.

snapshot.result: The response completes the enclosing interval. Overlapping child durations cannot be added as elapsed time.

transition.meaning: The response closes the enclosing observation window.

steps.title: End the separate client span on timeout
steps.explanation: A timeout settles the span boundary, leaving the operation unresolved.

snapshot.result: The separate client span has ended, but its external operation remains unresolved.

transition.meaning: A timeout settles the span boundary, leaving the operation unresolved.

steps.title: Correlate the late operation result
steps.explanation: The linked callback settles the operation outcome; it does not prove task acceptance.

snapshot.result: The correlated callback confirms the external effect; whole-task acceptance still needs its own evidence.

transition.meaning: The linked callback settles the operation outcome; it does not prove task acceptance.

invariants: Recorded span geometry stays fixed.
Synthesis cannot start until both tests and lint finish; the gap is unattributed.
Client timeout ends a span without establishing the external outcome.

title: Body loss does not erase a trial
question: What survives when a verdict arrives after body eviction?
scope: Two admitted toy trials A and B; two bounded body slots. Permitted minimized bodies only. Selection is intentionally diagnostic, with no claim that the retained set estimates population rates.

steps.title: Record every admitted trial
steps.explanation: The denominator is recorded before diagnostic retention.

snapshot.result: Both admitted trials exist in accounting before either diagnostic body is captured.

steps.title: Capture a permitted minimized batch
steps.explanation: Both bodies enter bounded staging; accounting is independent.

snapshot.result: The provisional bodies occupy bounded staging while their verdicts remain pending.

transition.meaning: Both bodies enter bounded staging; accounting is independent.

steps.title: Evict A before its verdict
steps.explanation: Pressure removes A’s body and records the diagnostic loss.

snapshot.result: A loses its diagnostic body, but its admitted-trial record and eviction flag persist.

transition.meaning: Pressure removes A’s body and records the diagnostic loss.

steps.title: Record A’s late failed verdict
steps.explanation: A remains a failed admitted trial even though its detailed body is gone.

snapshot.result: A is now a known failed trial with missing detail; the verdict cannot reconstruct its evicted body.

transition.meaning: A remains a failed admitted trial even though its detailed body is gone.

steps.title: Record B’s failed verdict
steps.explanation: B still has its permitted body and receives high diagnostic priority.

snapshot.result: B is a known failed trial whose body remains available for high-priority diagnostic retention.

transition.meaning: B still has its permitted body and receives high diagnostic priority.

steps.title: Copy B into retained storage
steps.explanation: The eligible body is copied with its inclusion record; staging survives the store write.

snapshot.result: B now has a retained copy and an inclusion record; its staging source remains until the store write is complete.

transition.meaning: The eligible body is copied with its inclusion record; staging survives the store write.

steps.title: Release B’s consumed staging slot
steps.explanation: The retained store write is complete, so its staging source can now be released.

snapshot.result: B’s staging slot is free after its final consumer. A’s missing body and both admitted-trial records remain visible.

transition.meaning: The retained store write is complete, so its staging source can now be released.

invariants: Every admitted trial stays in the accounting table after its body disappears.
A late verdict cannot reconstruct an evicted body.
Retention policy and inclusion record accompany retained diagnostics.

title: One credit spans all four responsibilities
question: Why does a finished rollout still hold collection capacity?
scope: Two toy credits and two admitted runs. Each credit covers one fixed payload ceiling; execution resources have separate bounds. The hard limit is demonstrated, not a quantitative watermark controller.

steps.title: Before admission
steps.explanation: The full collection capacity is available.

snapshot.result: The reservation pool is free; no record is admitted.

steps.title: Admit a bounded batch
steps.explanation: Atomic admission reserves one collection credit per run.

snapshot.result: Both runs now own a collection reservation before rollout begins.

transition.meaning: Atomic admission reserves one collection credit per run.

steps.title: Capture both completed rollouts
steps.explanation: This parallel capture retains each run’s existing reservation.

snapshot.result: Completed rollouts move into capture while keeping their existing reservations.

transition.meaning: This parallel capture retains each run’s existing reservation.

steps.title: Stage both captured records
steps.explanation: Moving responsibility changes the holding location without freeing capacity.

snapshot.result: The captured records move into staging; reservation ownership does not end at the stage boundary.

transition.meaning: Moving responsibility changes the holding location without freeing capacity.

steps.title: Begin downstream assessment
steps.explanation: Both runs occupy assessment while their reservations remain held.

snapshot.result: Assessment holds both records and both reservations, even though rollout has finished.

transition.meaning: Both runs occupy assessment while their reservations remain held.

steps.title: Reject an additional admission
steps.explanation: No collection reservation remains; the hard cap stops a new run.

snapshot.result: C cannot enter the pipeline because all collection capacity is still owned downstream.

transition.meaning: No collection reservation remains; the hard cap stops a new run.

steps.title: Confirm A’s durable disposition
steps.explanation: A leaves pending assessment; its credit remains held until the return is recorded.

snapshot.result: A has a confirmed durable disposition. Its reservation stays held until the explicit return is recorded.

transition.meaning: A leaves pending assessment; its credit remains held until the return is recorded.

steps.title: Return A’s collection credit
steps.explanation: Confirmed durable disposition authorizes this capacity release.

snapshot.result: A’s returned credit can admit another run while B continues to hold its own reservation.

transition.meaning: Confirmed durable disposition authorizes this capacity release.

invariants: Every nonterminal admitted run keeps a collection reservation across all stages.
Rollout completion alone returns no credit.
A credit returns only after a durable disposition is confirmed.

title: Leaked context changes the attention output
question: What contribution disappears when example B cannot read example A?
scope: Toy packed buffer with two tokens per example, one two-component B0 query, and scalar values. Dot products are unscaled toy logits. This score-row example makes no claim about skipped kernel work.

steps.title: Inspect independent packed examples
steps.explanation: B0 is the first query of the second example.

snapshot.result: B0 shares a physical buffer with A but belongs to a separate example.

steps.title: Compute the query–key score row
steps.explanation: Dot products produce candidate scores for the selected query.

snapshot.result: The unmasked score row contains both earlier-example keys and the future B1 key.

transition.meaning: Dot products produce candidate scores for the selected query.

steps.title: Apply ordinary causality
steps.explanation: Future B1 is excluded, but A0 and A1 retain finite scores.

snapshot.result: Ordinary causality removes future B1 but leaves finite scores for A’s unrelated context.

transition.meaning: Future B1 is excluded, but A0 and A1 retain finite scores.

steps.title: Normalize ordinary causal scores
steps.explanation: The first example receives nonzero probability mass.

snapshot.result: The ordinary softmax assigns nonzero weight to A’s values.

transition.meaning: The first example receives nonzero probability mass.

steps.title: Reduce values under ordinary causality
steps.explanation: Cross-example values now contribute to B0’s attention result.

snapshot.result: The ordinary attention output now contains a computed contribution from the unrelated example A.

transition.meaning: Cross-example values now contribute to B0’s attention result.

steps.title: Mask cross-example scores before softmax
steps.explanation: A0 and A1 become −∞; old weights are invalidated before recomputation.

snapshot.result: Cross-example scores become −∞ before normalization. The old weights are invalid and disappear.

transition.meaning: A0 and A1 become −∞; old weights are invalidated before recomputation.

steps.title: Normalize the example-isolated scores
steps.explanation: Only B0 remains finite, giving its value all probability mass.

snapshot.result: Only B0 retains probability mass; A can no longer influence this query’s value reduction.

transition.meaning: Only B0 remains finite, giving its value all probability mass.

steps.title: Reduce values within the example
steps.explanation: The isolated output keeps B0’s contribution and removes the first example’s contribution.

snapshot.result: The corrected result uses only B0’s value; the contaminated ordinary result remains alongside it for comparison.

transition.meaning: The isolated output keeps B0’s contribution and removes the first example’s contribution.

invariants: Packed inputs, query, keys, and values remain unchanged.
Causality excludes B1; membership separately excludes A0 and A1 before softmax.
The ordinary output includes value contributions from example A; the isolated output cannot.
Displayed weights are rounded for legibility; outputs use unrounded probabilities.

title: A passed record can still be stale
question: How does trainer progress change eligibility without changing a verdict?
scope: Focused toy admission case for the figure’s asynchronous path: three records sampled at versions 2, 1, and 0, trainer initially 3, maximum lag 2. It does not reproduce the four-member synchronous timing example or establish complete group eligibility.

steps.title: Rollouts run under fixed behavior versions
steps.explanation: The trainer is already ahead of these in-flight records.

snapshot.result: The rollout records retain their generating versions while the trainer is already ahead.

steps.title: Complete and verify A
steps.explanation: A’s environment slot frees; its compact verified record stays in the bounded buffer.

snapshot.result: A’s environment slot is free, but its verified compact record stays buffered for admission.

transition.meaning: A’s environment slot frees; its compact verified record stays in the bounded buffer.

steps.title: Check A at the current trainer version
steps.explanation: A passes the record-level lag gate; group closure remains a separate obligation.

snapshot.result: A satisfies the record-level lag gate. This does not close a planned training cohort.

transition.meaning: A passes the record-level lag gate; group closure remains a separate obligation.

steps.title: Commit one trainer update
steps.explanation: The trainer advances while B and C retain their original behavior versions.

snapshot.result: One trainer update increases the lag of every fixed behavior version without changing any verdict.

transition.meaning: The trainer advances while B and C retain their original behavior versions.

steps.title: Complete and verify B
steps.explanation: B has a pass verdict, independently of its current lag.

snapshot.result: B has a pass verdict and a free environment slot; freshness eligibility is still unchecked.

transition.meaning: B has a pass verdict, independently of its current lag.

steps.title: Exclude B by the lag bound
steps.explanation: The verified record exceeds the version bound; its reason remains recorded.

snapshot.result: B’s verified record is excluded as stale, and the reason remains in the ledger.

transition.meaning: The verified record exceeds the version bound; its reason remains recorded.

steps.title: Complete and verify C
steps.explanation: The final environment slot frees; the older record still has its generating version.

snapshot.result: C’s completed environment slot is free; its older generating version still belongs to the buffered record.

transition.meaning: The final environment slot frees; the older record still has its generating version.

steps.title: Exclude C by the lag bound
steps.explanation: A pass verdict does not override the recorded freshness limit.

snapshot.result: C is also excluded by lag. A pass verdict does not override the freshness bound.

transition.meaning: A pass verdict does not override the recorded freshness limit.

invariants: Each record keeps the version that generated it.
A rollout completion frees an environment slot while its record remains buffered.
Verified rewards, lag eligibility, and complete cohort eligibility are separate checks.

title: A checked candidate still needs a head guard
question: Why can a clean and tested candidate fail publication?
scope: Symbolic repository example using disjoint interface and caller files. Hash labels identify exact states rather than real commits. A target-head change invalidates the publication attempt; no external effects are rolled back.

steps.title: Begin with private caller work
steps.explanation: The caller depends on interface v1 at the common base.

snapshot.result: The private caller depends on the original interface at the common base.

steps.title: Publish an independent interface change
steps.explanation: The target interface becomes v2 while the private caller still requires v1.

snapshot.result: The target interface changes while the private caller still expects the older contract.

transition.meaning: The target interface becomes v2 while the private caller still requires v1.

steps.title: Build a textually clean candidate
steps.explanation: Disjoint file edits merge, but the combined candidate retains a stale dependency.

snapshot.result: Candidate c1 merges without a text conflict but carries an unsupported caller dependency.

transition.meaning: Disjoint file edits merge, but the combined candidate retains a stale dependency.

steps.title: Revise the private caller dependency
steps.explanation: The worker adapts its caller to the current interface; old candidate c1 is unchanged.

snapshot.result: The private caller now targets v2; candidate c1 remains unchanged and still needs rebuilding.

transition.meaning: The worker adapts its caller to the current interface; old candidate c1 is unchanged.

steps.title: Build a revised integration candidate
steps.explanation: Candidate c2 captures h1 and carries the revised caller.

snapshot.result: Candidate c2 captures h1 with the revised caller; it needs evidence of its own.

transition.meaning: Candidate c2 captures h1 and carries the revised caller.

steps.title: Validate and test exact candidate c2
steps.explanation: One bounded validation job checks declared dependencies and executes the required candidate tests.

snapshot.result: The required checks support exact candidate c2 against captured head h1.

transition.meaning: One bounded validation job checks declared dependencies and executes the required candidate tests.

steps.title: Advance the target before publication
steps.explanation: An intervening accepted update changes the target from captured head h1.

snapshot.result: The target advances to h2 after c2 was checked; the old candidate evidence does not cover the new head.

transition.meaning: An intervening accepted update changes the target from captured head h1.

steps.title: Attempt the expected-head update
steps.explanation: The atomic guard observes h2 rather than h1 and refuses publication.

snapshot.result: The expected-head update refuses publication and returns to revalidation; h2 remains the target.

transition.meaning: The atomic guard observes h2 rather than h1 and refuses publication.

invariants: Textual merge success does not establish semantic dependency compatibility.
Tests name the exact integration candidate they evaluated.
Atomic publication requires the captured head and all publication guards to hold.

title: Stopping preserves the child’s backing
question: Which event allows the root to reuse a canceled child’s funds?
scope: The chapter’s hypothetical budget records in integer milli-dollars, not provider prices. Starts after both child allocations and local charges are recorded. The child view and root reservation are the same backing seen at two levels.

steps.title: Both allocations remain backed
steps.explanation: The trace and fuzz children have local charge records; root reserves their complete allocations.

partition.status: Balance partition geometry changes with account transfers

snapshot.result: The root reserves both complete child allocations while the fuzz child separately tracks its own pending remote liability.

steps.title: Close the fully settled trace child
steps.explanation: The trace child returns only its unused allocation and posts its settled charge to the root.

partition.status: Balance partition geometry changes with account transfers

snapshot.result: The settled trace child closes; only its unused funds return to the root’s free balance.

transition.meaning: The trace child returns only its unused allocation and posts its settled charge to the root.

steps.title: Stop the fuzz child locally
steps.explanation: New spending admission closes; the remote reservation and whole root backing remain.

partition.status: Balance partition geometry changes with account transfers

snapshot.result: The fuzz child stops admitting work. Its remote liability and complete root reservation remain unchanged.

transition.meaning: New spending admission closes; the remote reservation and whole root backing remain.

steps.title: Settle the authenticated late bill
steps.explanation: The child consumes its bounded remote reservation; the root still backs the open child.

partition.status: Balance partition geometry changes with account transfers

snapshot.result: Authenticated final billing settles the child’s remote liability; the root still backs the open child account.

transition.meaning: The child consumes its bounded remote reservation; the root still backs the open child.

steps.title: Close the fully settled fuzz child
steps.explanation: No remote reservation remains; root imports the final charge and returns only unused funds.

partition.status: Balance partition geometry changes with account transfers

snapshot.result: The fully settled fuzz child closes. Its final charge reaches the root and only its unused funds become free.

transition.meaning: No remote reservation remains; root imports the final charge and returns only unused funds.

invariants: At every node, settled plus reserved plus free equals its own allocation.
A parent reservation and the backed child account must not be added together as spending.
Stopping closes admission but releases no remote liability.
Only authenticated final settlement, followed by child closure, returns uncommitted funds to the root.
